title: Licensed on-prem ops credits + upgrade path experiment
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Objective: Run a controlled experiment to validate a new packaging model for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that separates a recurring license fee from a finite pool of 'ops credits' used for upgrades, emergency patches, and premium support actions. We aim to find a balance that reduces sticker shock for large initial commitments while preserving predictable revenue and clear upgrade entitlements.

Hypothesis: Customers prefer a lower base license with purchasable ops credit bundles (monthly/annual) for operational activities (scheduled upgrades, emergency hotfixes, assisted upgrades, and out-of-band support). This will increase adoption velocity for mid-market accounts and create predictable add-on revenue for enterprise.

Experiment arms: 
- Arm A (Baseline): Current model (flat license + inclusive upgrades/support as historically sold).
- Arm B (Ops Credits): Lower base license (~15-25% reduction) + ops credit bundles (S/M/L) that cover upgrade windows, one assisted upgrade per year, and emergency SLA fast-tracks.
- Arm C (Hybrid Commitment): Flat license with optional ops credit pool discount when committing to 12 months of reserved capacity.

Key metrics: conversion rate from evaluation -> POC -> contract signed, average deal value (ACV), time-to-first-deploy for on-prem customers, frequency of emergency upgrade purchases, churn at renewal, sales cycle length, NPS on upgrade/patching experience.

Success criteria: 10%+ lift in mid-market conversion within 90 days for Arm B vs Baseline OR equal conversion with 8% uplift in ACV. Ops credit revenue should show >5% of total private revenue in pilot accounts without increasing churn.

Scope and constraints: pilot limited to 12 customers across Finance and Healthcare segments where security questionnaire friction is high. Legal must validate contract language for entitlement mapping. SRE/Eng must provide an upgrade automation SLA matrix and estimate average ops credit burn rates per upgrade class. Pricing must be compatible with marketplace listing and existing enterprise discounts.

Deliverables: pricing sheet, contracting playbook language, entitlement matrix, sales FAQ, support routing playbook, dashboard to track ops credit consumption by account, and a short SDK/tooling checklist for assisted upgrades.

Risks: perceived nickel-and-diming for long-term customers, complexity in quoting, increased support load if ops credits are priced incorrectly, and potential conflicts with existing contractual upgrade guarantees.

Timeline: 4-week design & legal review, 6-week pilot sales effort, 6-week data collection + analysis. Rollup decision to Exec in Q2.

Artifacts: Confluence brief: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/PM-34721-Ops-Credits, Pricing mock (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1OpsCreditsMock, Draft contract language (Legal): https://legal.redwood.ai/drafts/ops-credits-draft-v1.pdf, Pilot customer list (internal spreadsheet): https://sheets.redwood.ai/d/PrivateOpsPilot
